rules.title: Newark Rent Control: annual rent increases limited to CPI-U percentage
rules.requirement: Landlords of rent-controlled units may raise rent annually only by the monthly published CPI-U percentage, with 30 days' advance written notice. Increases above that require Rent Control Board approval for hardship, major improvements, or tax and utility surcharges.
rules.key_value: Annual increase capped at CPI-U % for the month of increase (e.g., 2.6% May 2017); 0% during COVID moratorium Apr 2020–Sept 2023
rules.coverage_conditions: Residential rental dwellings in Newark under the Rent Control Ordinance.
rules.exemptions: Public housing; motel or hotel space rented day to day; commercial space. New multiple dwellings can be exempt for 30 years if the owner gets a certificate of exemption before occupancy. Substantially rehabilitated dwellings can be exempt for 5 years (if previously vacant 18 months) or 1 year (initial rent) with Board certificate.

coverage.unverifiable_conditions: The 30-year new-construction exemption applies only if the owner applied for a certificate of exemption before occupancy. Substantial-rehabilitation exemptions require a Board certificate.

rules.penalty: Tenant may file a rent adjustment application with the Rent Control Board.
rules.citation: Newark Rent Control Ordinance (Newark Municipal Code)
rules.quoted_span:
permissible annual rent increases for a given month are shown in the table  below. Landlords may 
increase rents as per the Consumer Price Index - Urban percentage (CPI-U %) published every 
month.
rules.conflict_note: Before June 20, 2014 the caps were 4% (50+ units) and 5% (49 or fewer units). The ordinance was passed in 1973 and its latest overhaul took effect Sept 11, 2019. A COVID moratorium (MEO-20-0004) froze increases from Apr 1, 2020 until it was rescinded Sept 18, 2023, with 0% calculation for that period. The FAQ gives no specific code chapter citation. The 30-year new-construction exemption comes from state statute and requires an application, so the age-based exemption is not automatic. The CPI table ends in early 2024.

rules.title: Newark Rent Control: registration required before rent increases
rules.requirement: Owners must register their properties with the Division of Rent Control, and an unregistered landlord may not increase rent.
rules.coverage_conditions: Owners of rental properties covered by the Newark Rent Control Ordinance.
rules.exemptions: Same exemptions as the Rent Control Ordinance (public housing, transient hotel/motel, commercial, exempted new construction or rehabilitation).
rules.penalty: The Board may deny an increase if the property is not registered.
rules.citation: Newark Rent Control Ordinance (Newark Municipal Code)
rules.quoted_span: Your landlord must register with the Division of Rent Control in order to increase rents.

rules.title: Newark Rent Control: no eviction in reprisal for enforcing rent control rights
rules.requirement: A landlord may not bring an action to recover possession of a unit in retaliation for a tenant's efforts to enforce rights under the Rent Control Ordinance, such as filing a petition.
rules.coverage_conditions: Tenants of units covered by the Newark Rent Control Ordinance.
rules.citation: Newark Rent Control Ordinance (Newark Municipal Code)
rules.quoted_span:
Your landlord shall not bring action to recover possession of your apartment as a reprisal of 
your efforts to enforce your rights under Rent Control.
rules.conflict_note: Source is an FAQ summary. NJ state anti-reprisal and Anti-Eviction Act protections also apply, but this document does not cite them.
